title: Contextual postmortem scaffold and adjustable action templates
author: Leah Park
description: Add a lightweight, context-aware postmortem scaffold and a set of adjustable action-item templates for on-call responders. Motivation: reduce friction in creating consistent incident reports and accelerate assignment of remediation tasks by surfacing templated, severity-aware actions derived from telemetry and runbook context. This PR introduces a JSON/YAML-backed scaffold generator that the incident-bot can populate from alert context (service, error class, paging timeline) and a small DSL for action templates (severity, owner-suggest, estimated-effort, auto-followup). Checklist: - [x] add scaffold generator and template registry - [x] wire scaffold generation into /incidents/new endpoint - [x] add CLI helper (ibot postmortem --scaffold) - [x] add unit tests for template rendering - [x] update docs with examples and recommended postmortem checklist Notes: the description field for generated postmortems is intentionally compact and includes links to the relevant runbooks and traces. Templates are configurable per-team via Git-backed config in .incident-bot/templates. This approach keeps the incident creation path fast while ensuring consistent capture of root-cause evidence and mitigation steps. Related: ENG-4123 (postmortem UX improvements), OPS-98 (oncall playbook harmonization).

review_thread: Diego Martinez: Nice - this addresses the repeated friction we've seen when creating PMs after incidents. Two asks: 1) add a small knob to opt-out of auto-suggested owners, 2) ensure the templates do not leak internal trace URLs for non-privileged teams.

Leah Park: replied: added optOutOwners flag and sanitized links via runbook-linker (see internal/postmortem/sanitize.go). Templates default to suggested owners but teams can override in their repo config.
Aisha Patel: requested: add an example of a short-form postmortem for SEV3 (one-paragraph) to docs. Also suggested making estimated-effort a human-friendly phrase ("~2hrs") rather than just minutes.
Leah Park: replied: updated templates and docs; effort now supports humanized strings and ISO minutes.
notes_on_backward_compatibility: Templates live under .incident-bot/templates and the default registry is seeded. Existing saved postmortems are unchanged; the generator only runs when callers opt into the scaffold endpoint or CLI. No runtime schema changes for persisted incident records.
security_considerations: Sanitized sensitive links and removed stack dumps from default scaffold. Teams can opt-in to include raw traces if they have appropriate access. Audit logs emitted for template rendering requests.
release_notes: Add contextual postmortem scaffold and team-configurable action templates; CLI helper for rapid postmortem creation. Improves on-call efficiency and consistency of incident reports.
merge_outcome: merged via squash (maintainer: Ravi Sundaram). Post-merge: backed by small rollout flag (POSTMORTEM_SCAFFOLD=true) disabled by default; ops will enable for internal SRE first week after merge. Migration: none required.
